summary: Josh Purtell, founder of Synth Labs, shares patterns for building stateful environments for vertical agents targeting domains like finance, accounting, and health. The concept of "environments" has deep roots in reinforcement learning, where tasks are containerized separately from the AI algorithm. Historical implementations include RL Glue, OpenAI Gym (from when OpenAI was an RL company), and more recently SWE-bench/SWE-agent's "agent-computer interface." The motivation for adding statefulness now stems from model improvements. Two years ago, LLMs performed simple tool use needing few abstractions. As models improved—particularly with Sonnet 3.5—and Claude artifacts emerged, people began thinking about products/artifacts that agents iterate on over long horizons, necessitating cleaner abstractions. A stateful environment is defined as an engine computing results external to the agent implementation. The agent manipulates the environment, but underlying logic (API access, Excel manipulation, external sources of truth) is encapsulated. The environment exposes a representation the agent can observe and manipulate—showing only what is needed rather than the entire OS. Network boundaries separate the agent process from the environment, enabling multi-agent settings and RL training. Key benefits include: containerizing vertical app logic into stable code makes it easier to revamp agents when new models arrive; network boundaries enable reliable asynchronous multi-agent work in production; reset and rollback capabilities allow recovering from derailed agents; and resettable environments enable techniques like language agent tree search for free—branching agents, evaluating, and converging on the best branch, valuable in long-horizon settings like Minecraft with hundreds or thousands of steps. An open-source GitHub repository (synth-laboratories/Environments) implements these abstractions across academic benchmarks including Pokemon Red, Minecraft, and SWE-Bench.

sections.title: Introduction and motivation for stateful environments
sections.summary: Josh Purtell introduces himself as founder of Synth Labs and explains he helps people improve their agents. He has found patterns for structuring agent code that are helpful for vertical applications like finance, accounting, and health, which he calls stateful environments—environments that capture state for the agent.

sections.title: History of environments in reinforcement learning
sections.summary: Purtell traces the concept of environments through RL history: RL Glue as the first implementation, OpenAI Gym (from when OpenAI was an RL company), and SWE-bench/SWE-agent's agent-computer interface. He frames this as building on existing work rather than reinventing the wheel.

sections.title: Why now: the impetus for stateful abstractions
sections.summary: Two years ago LLMs performed simple tool use needing few abstractions. As models improved with API-based tool use and MCP excitement, and particularly with Sonnet 3.5 and Claude artifacts, people began thinking about products/artifacts agents iterate on over long horizons, creating the need for stateful environment abstractions.

sections.title: Definition of a stateful environment
sections.summary: A stateful environment is an engine that computes results external to the agent implementation. It exposes a representation or version of the environment the agent can observe and manipulate—showing only what is needed rather than the entire OS. Network boundaries separate the agent process from the environment, useful for RL training and multi-agent settings.

sections.title: Benefits: revamping, multi-agent, rollback, and tree search
sections.summary: Containerizing vertical app logic into stable code makes it easier to revamp agents when new models arrive. Network boundaries enable reliable asynchronous multi-agent work. Reset and rollback let you recover derailed agents. Resettable environments enable language agent tree search for free—branching in games like Minecraft, evaluating branches, and converging on the best one.

sections.title: GitHub repository and conclusion
sections.summary: Purtell directs listeners to an open-source GitHub repository (synth AI environments / synth-laboratories/Environments) that captures these abstractions with implementations across academic benchmarks including Pokemon Red, Minecraft, and SWE-Bench.

demonstrations: Screenshot of a tree-search step where an agent branched in two directions while playing Minecraft, with one branch performing better
limitations: The language agent tree search paper was nearly impossible to implement in production due to lack of good abstractions
